lines.li: The droid's tone shifts, almost too low to hear. It doesn't say why.
Something in the walls just changed pitch. The droid noticed before you did.
"That second tone," the droid says. "That one is new. I don't like that one."
The droid stops what it's doing and listens. It doesn't start again for a while.
"Three tones now." The droid's voice has gone flat. "I would like to stop soon."
The droid backs itself against a wall, facing outward, and stays there.
The hum just stopped. The droid isn't moving either. "Why have you angered this place?" it asks no one.
Total silence, all at once. The droid says nothing at all -- which is worse.
The drone here is flat as a dead battery. The droid says it has never heard a place sound so empty.
Nothing in the hum rises or falls. The droid taps its own casing, as if to check that it is the one still working.
"It sounds like nothing lives here," the droid says. It does not sound relieved.
The drone has not changed. The droid keeps turning its head toward it anyway.
The droid's servos tick and settle, tick and settle, like a held breath. It cannot say what for.
"Same tone as before," the droid reports. A pause. "It does not feel like the same tone."
The hum is as dull as ever. The droid has gone quiet in a way that is not dull at all.
The droid stops mid-step, listens to the flat drone, and decides not to finish the step.
"Nothing has changed," the droid says, too quickly.
The drone holds one flat note. The droid has pressed itself to the nearest wall and will not say why.
The droid's photoreceptors dim to their lowest setting. "I do not hear anything new," it says. "I would like to leave."
"The sound is the same," the droid insists. Its hands will not stop shaking.
The drone drones on, flat and dull. The droid has frozen beside it and will not move for anyone.
"Nothing is different," the droid whispers. "Everything is different. I cannot hear where."
The droid has powered down everything but its eyes. The hum has not changed at all.
The hum has settled into one warm drone. The droid's shoulders, such as they are, come down.
"There," the droid says, as the tones thin back to one. "That is the good one."
One low tone again, steady under the plating. The droid goes back to work humming along, slightly off-key.
A thin second note slides in under the drone. The droid pauses, tilts its head, and carries on more carefully.
"Did you feel that?" the droid asks, one hand flat on the deck. "Just there. Gone again."
The pitch under your feet lifts a hair. The droid recalibrates its audio and does not comment further.
Two tones now, rubbing against each other. The droid winds its movements down to half speed.
"I preferred the quiet," the droid says. "The other quiet. The warm one."
The droid sets down what it was carrying, very gently, and waits for the second tone to pass.
Three tones, grinding. The droid has backed into a corner and is counting something under its breath.
"This is the part where we stop," the droid says, and offers no reason.
The droid's vocabulator crackles twice before any words come out. "Too loud. Too many."
Every tone drops out at once. The droid freezes mid-motion and stays that way.
Dead silence on the plating. The droid does not move, does not speak, does not look at you.
"Stop," the droid says into the silence. "Everyone. Please. Stop."
The drone is warm today. The droid says the ground here has been easier lately, and leaves it at that.
One soft tone, steady as breathing. The droid powers down to idle without being told.
"I like it here, now," the droid admits, then looks surprised at itself.
A second note rises and falls away again. The droid hardly breaks stride.
The hum shivers once. "Only a shiver," the droid says. "They pass, lately."
The droid pauses at the new tone, then keeps on. It has heard this one before and come through it.
Two tones again. The droid slows down. "It has been a while since that one," it says.
The second tone holds. The droid puts its tools away one at a time, neatly, the way it does when it is nervous.
"I had forgotten how that sounds," the droid says quietly. "I would rather not remember it."
Three tones, sharp ones. The droid stands very still. "It had been easier," it says. "This is not easier."
The droid backs toward the nearest wall without taking its eyes off the deck plates.
"Whatever we just did," the droid says, "I would like us not to do it again."
The hum cuts out entirely. After so long, the silence is worse. The droid locks in place.
Silence, everywhere at once. The droid lowers itself to the plating and does not get up.
"No," the droid says, very small, into the quiet. "Not after all this time."
One warm tone. The droid rests a hand on the deck the way you might rest a hand on a sleeping animal's flank.
"It knows we are here," the droid says, quite calmly. "I can feel it knowing. Right now that is all right."
The drone settles low and wide. The droid has stopped whispering on these plates; it seems sure it will be heard either way.
A second tone rises under the plating. "Attention," the droid says, in the voice of something being looked at.
The droid lifts its head at the new note, like a pupil hearing its name. It does not say what it heard.
"It is listening harder," the droid murmurs. "I cannot tell you to what."
Two tones. The droid goes still. "So big," it says. "I keep forgetting how big, until it does that."
"It is not pleased," the droid says. "I do not know with what. Neither of us is going to ask."
The droid steps carefully off the plates under it, apologizing to the floor.
Three tones. The droid presses both hands to the deck. "It is all of this," it whispers. "Under everything. And it is upset."
"I know what it feels," the droid says. "I still do not know what it wants. I would like it to stop feeling it."
The droid stops talking mid-word, the way you stop when something enormous turns to look.
Silence, across the whole plateau at once. The droid has seen what lies under it. It does not move.
The hum is gone. "It has stopped saying anything," the droid says. "That is the worst thing it says."
"We know what it feels," the droid says into the silence. "Now so do you."
